critic.rationale: The plan for R-003 (crypto-domain config and diagnostics parity) is well-structured and passes all rubric checks. The design_contract explicitly defines both persistence_protocol (read-only Redis via HotViewReadService, no writes from app-api) and concurrency_protocol (stateless request-scoped domain resolution, no shared mutable state). All five affected surfaces—web controllers, service layer, redis layer, test suite, and UI tests—are covered by at least one slice's allowed_paths. No slice contains self-overlap between its own allowed_paths and forbidden_paths; cross-role boundaries are correctly used (e.g. impl-primary forbids test paths that qa-author owns). All implementer and QA slices carry explicit Gradle or shell verification commands. The acceptance_test_matrix and risk_register together cover stale/TTL-expired key handling (pass-through, HTTP 200), missing/null key defaults (safe empty value), and equities backward-compatibility invariants. implementation_topology is 'single' and only one engineering.implement slice (impl-primary) exists—no topology conflict. The slice dependency chain is linear and acyclic: design → qa-author → impl-primary → review → qa-verify, so no non-terminal slice is orphaned and qa-author precedes impl while qa-verify follows review. finalization_policy is 'open_final_feature_pr_for_human_merge', preserving human gate. All objectives name concrete files, methods, and test classes. A seven-entry risk_register is present. R-003 declares no upstream dependencies in the roadmap and the plan reflects none, so roadmap dependency handling is trivially satisfied. The plan introduces only stateless read-path branching with no new mutable state or Redis writes, preserving app-api's allocation-light, read-only hot-path invariant. The feature spans multiple surfaces (config controller, diagnostics controller, service, redis, Playwright) so the small-feature compactness constraint does not apply, and the five-slice structure is the minimum required given mandatory qa-author, reviewer, and qa-verify checks.
